data.answer: This walks the import graph backwards from auto_ontology/semantic/constants.py, collecting every file that imports it directly or indirectly, and collapses the traversal to distinct file paths so repeated or cyclic import chains are not double-counted. It then keeps only non-test files, derives each file's top-level package directory from the first two path segments of the repository-relative path, and counts the distinct files in each directory. Results are grouped by that package area and ordered by file count from highest to lowest, with ties broken alphabetically by area.

display_annotations.note: Deterministic display links; not source citations made by the model.

output_contract.guidance: Return the package-directory area and file count. Order by files descending, then area ascending.

data.question: Which files import, directly or through other files, auto_ontology/semantic/constants.py? Give the number of such non-test files per top-level package directory.
data.reference_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE importers(file_id) AS (
  SELECT i.file_id FROM code.imports i
  WHERE i.imported_file_id = 'auto_ontology/semantic/constants.py'
  UNION
  SELECT i.file_id FROM code.imports i
  JOIN importers m ON i.imported_file_id = m.file_id
)
SELECT split_part(f.file_id, '/', 1) || '/' || split_part(f.file_id, '/', 2) AS area,
       COUNT(*) AS files
FROM importers m
JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = m.file_id
WHERE NOT f.is_test
GROUP BY area
ORDER BY files DESC, area;

request.evidence: Follow resolved imports backwards, recursively. The top-level package directory is the first two path segments.
request.question:
Which files import, directly or through other files, auto_ontology/semantic/constants.py? Give the number of such non-test files per top-level package directory.

Requested output columns: area (string), files (integer).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. After executing SQL, describe the returned rows and query assumptions. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. Use files.is_test for test-file classification; test_links describe associations, not the complete set of test files. Use DOUBLE or DECIMAL, rather than single-precision REAL, for percentage calculations.
Return the package-directory area and file count. Order by files descending, then area ascending.

data.sql: WITH RECURSIVE importers(file_id) AS (SELECT i.file_id FROM auto_ontology_code.code.imports AS i WHERE i.imported_file_id = 'auto_ontology/semantic/constants.py' UNION SELECT i.file_id FROM importers AS r JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.imports AS i ON i.imported_file_id = r.file_id) SELECT CASE WHEN split_part(f.file_id, '/', 2) = '' THEN split_part(f.file_id, '/', 1) ELSE split_part(f.file_id, '/', 1) || '/' || split_part(f.file_id, '/', 2) END AS area, COUNT(DISTINCT f.file_id) AS files FROM importers AS r JOIN auto_ontology_code.code.files AS f ON f.file_id = r.file_id WHERE f.is_test = false GROUP BY area ORDER BY files DESC, area ASC
